extensive or fulminant disease intravenous corticosteroids should be given.3,5,6 Add- ing intravenous metronidazole may be advisable, be- cause of the difficulty of distinguishing active disease from a septic complication.3 Infliximab should be considered in patients with disease refractory to cor- ticosteroids;3,5,6 adalimumab or certolizumab pegol may be alternatives.6 • fistulising disease Simple perianal fistulae can be treated with metroni- dazole or ciprofloxacin.3,6 Azathioprine or mercap- topurine are also potentially effective,3 while inflixi- mab is recommended in patients who do not respond to other treatment.3,6 An alternative to infliximab is adalimumab.6 Surgery is appropriate for complex or persistent fistulae.3,6 • chronic active and corticosteroid dependent disease Azathioprine or mercaptopurine are the drugs of choice in corticosteroid dependent disease.3 If they are ineffective or not tolerated, intramuscular meth- otrexate may be considered;5 it is also considered ap- propriate for the management of chronic active dis- ease.3 Infliximab is generally reserved for patients who fail first-line therapy, as an alternative to surgical resection.3 • MAINTENANCE: The most important intervention in maintaining re- mission in patients with Crohn’s disease is probably to persuade those who smoke to stop smoking.3 Mesalazine appears to be of limited benefit at best for the maintenance of remission,3,5,10,40 although it is widely used,6 and the other aminosalicylates are con- sidered inappropriate.3,5 Corticosteroids are also not effective for maintenance,3,5,12 although budesonide may delay relapse for a limited period.5,6 In patients who required corticosteroids to achieve remission, the usual drug treatment for maintenance is a thiopu- rine (azathioprine or mercaptopurine).3,5,6 In patients who achieved remission with intramuscular meth- otrexate, it may be continued for maintenance;3 it is also an option in patients intolerant of thiopurines.5 Thiopurine maintenance may need to be continued for several years,5 or even indefinitely.6 Infliximab is also an option for maintenance, particularly in pa- tients brought to remission with the same drug,3,5 or those who cannot maintain remission or who remain corticosteroid dependent despite the use of mainte- nance immunosuppression.6 Alternatives may be adalimumab or certolizumab pegol.6 The use of ome- ga-3 fatty acids (fish oils) has been investigated for maintenance of remission in Crohn’s disease, with some apparent benefit.32 1.
